question: What does drydock do each physics timestep in real time?
tldr: Move frames across buses until the step is due, then step physics.
answer: Between two physics steps, drydock waits on every bus at once, moves frames across each bus as long as their bits take, and hands arrived frames to the motors, whose answers queue on the same bus. When the timestep is due, every motor runs its law and MuJoCo steps once.
why: The loop interleaves two clocks (bus time and physics time) inside one function; the picture shows which happens inside the inner loop and which once per step.
rate: every physics timestep of the wall clock, usually 1 ms

nodes.label: main
nodes.tldr: Load robot file, open buses, pick clock
nodes.explain: Reads the robot file and scenario, builds the simulated robot (Drydock), opens each SocketCAN socket, serial pty and EtherCAT socket, then runs the real-time or lockstep loop.

nodes.label: wait_any
nodes.tldr: Sleep until a socket is readable or an event
nodes.explain: One poll over all buses' file descriptors, woken by the earliest of: the next step being due, or the next frame finishing on a bus timeline.

nodes.label: read the masters' frames
nodes.tldr: Queue received frames on their bus timeline
nodes.explain: CAN frames and serial bytes are pushed onto their bus's timeline, ready now. EtherCAT frames skip the timeline: they pass through the drives at once and go straight back.

nodes.label: Timeline::advance
nodes.tldr: Frames whose bits have crossed by now
nodes.explain: Each bus lets one frame across at a time, lowest CAN id first (arbitration), for as long as its bits take, stuffing included. Serial lines do the same with bytes at the baud rate.

nodes.label: deliver to motors
nodes.tldr: Firmware handles frame, answer queued after reply delay
nodes.explain: An arrived master frame goes to the motor it's addressed to; its answer is queued on the same bus, ready reply_us later. An arrived motor answer is written to the master's socket.

nodes.label: Drydock::step
nodes.tldr: Motor laws, drivetrains, supply, then MuJoCo steps
nodes.explain: Once the timestep is due: faults are applied, each motor's law turns its latest command into a torque, the drivetrain limits it and puts it on the joint, and MuJoCo steps once.

nodes.label: report
nodes.tldr: Log faults and busy buses, write trace
nodes.explain: Prints what the scenario broke or restored, writes it to the trace, and once a second says if a bus is close to full. Falling over 100 ms behind is said and forgiven.

nodes.label: world + bus queues
nodes.tldr: Robot state and frames still crossing
nodes.explain: Carried from step to step: MuJoCo's joint state, each motor's latest command and registers, and each bus's queue of frames waiting or on the wire.

nodes.label: killed
nodes.tldr: Runs until stopped or an I/O error
nodes.explain: The loop never returns on its own; it ends on Ctrl-C or when a socket fails.
